s: With reference to the composition of a State Legislative Council, which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Local authorities — One-third of the total membership
Registered graduates — One-sixth of the total membership
Teachers — One-third of the total membership
Members nominated by the Governor — One-twelfth of the total membership
x: One-third of the members of a Legislative Council are elected by local authorities. Graduates and teachers each elect one-twelfth, while the Governor nominates one-sixth.
tq: Start from the sure fraction and eliminate the swapped fractions.
sec: Legislative Council composition - elected fractions, nominated, size, tenure

s: The members of a State Legislative Council elected by registered graduates must represent graduates who have been on the electoral roll for at least
x: One-twelfth of a State Legislative Council is elected by registered graduates having at least three years' standing.
tq: Distinguish the closely related three-year qualifications in the composition rules.
sec: Legislative Council composition - elected fractions, nominated, size, tenure

s: The electorate consisting of teachers for a State Legislative Council comprises teachers who have taught for at least three years in institutions
x: One-twelfth of the Council is elected by teachers with at least three years' teaching experience in institutions not lower than the secondary-school level.
tq: Test the exact official qualification instead of a broader everyday meaning of teacher.
sec: Legislative Council composition - elected fractions, nominated, size, tenure

s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the fields from which the Governor may nominate members to a State Legislative Council?
x: The nominated category includes literature, science, art, cooperative movement and social service. Agriculture taxation is not one of the constitutional fields.
tq: Find the outsider in the constitutionally specified list.
sec: Legislative Council composition - elected fractions, nominated, size, tenure

s:
Consider the following statements regarding nomination to a State Legislative Council:
1. The Governor nominates one-sixth of the total members.
2. The nominated members represent literature, science, art, cooperative movement and social service.
3. Such nominations are made on the advice of the State Cabinet.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The Governor nominates one-sixth of the Council from the specified fields, and the nominations are made on Cabinet advice.
tq: Check the fraction, the listed fields and the authority's advice together.
sec: Legislative Council composition - elected fractions, nominated, size, tenure

s: The members of a State Legislative Council are elected by which method?
o: Cumulative voting by the Legislative Assembly alone
First-past-the-post system by direct universal suffrage
Proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote
x: Members of a State Legislative Council are elected indirectly through proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.
tq: Discriminate between the electoral system and the appointing authority.
sec: Legislative Council composition - elected fractions, nominated, size, tenure

s:
With reference to the size of a State Legislative Council, which of the following statements are correct?
1. Its membership cannot exceed one-third of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly.
2. Its membership cannot be less than 40.
3. Its actual strength is fixed by Parliament.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: A Legislative Council must have at least 40 members and cannot exceed one-third of the Assembly's strength. Parliament fixes its actual strength within these limits.
tq: Combine the two numerical limits with the authority that fixes the actual size.
sec: Legislative Council composition - elected fractions, nominated, size, tenure

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the tenure of the State Legislative Council?
o: It is a permanent body, and one-sixth of its members retire every year.
It is a permanent body, and one-third of its members retire every second year.
It is dissolved every five years along with the Assembly.
It has a fixed tenure of six years as a whole House.
x: The Legislative Council is a permanent House. One-third of its members retire every second year, while each member has a six-year term.
tq: Separate the tenure of an individual member from the continuity of the House.
sec: Legislative Council composition - elected fractions, nominated, size, tenure

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Legislative Assembly from the Legislative Council in relation to a Money Bill?
o: A Money Bill may originate in either House, but the Council has the final decision.
The Council may reject a Money Bill if two-thirds of its members so decide.
A Money Bill can originate only in the Council on the Governor's recommendation.
A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Assembly, and the Council may make recommendations within 14 days.
x: A Money Bill is introduced only in the Legislative Assembly on the Governor's recommendation. The Council can only recommend changes and must return it within 14 days; it cannot reject or amend it.
tq: Identify who introduces, who recommends and who has the final word.
sec: Assembly vs Council - money bills, ordinary bills, delaying power, no joint sitting

s: In a State Legislature, the certificate that a Bill is a Money Bill is issued by the
x: Under Article 199(3), the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly certifies whether a Bill is a Money Bill.
tq: Apply the 'who would do this job?' method to the certification power.
sec: Assembly vs Council - money bills, ordinary bills, delaying power, no joint sitting

s: A Money Bill passed by the Legislative Assembly of a State is returned by the Legislative Council after 14 days with recommendations. What is the constitutional position?
o: The Governor decides which recommendations are binding.
The Bill lapses and must be introduced again.
The Assembly may accept or reject the recommendations.
The Assembly must accept all the recommendations.
x: The Council can only make recommendations on a Money Bill. The Assembly may accept or reject them, and the Council has no power to make its recommendations binding.
tq: Follow the Bill's route and distinguish recommendation from amendment power.
sec: Assembly vs Council - money bills, ordinary bills, delaying power, no joint sitting

s: An ordinary Bill passed by the Legislative Assembly and rejected by the Legislative Council is
o: Sent to Parliament for final decision
Automatically rejected by the State Legislature
Referred to a joint sitting of both Houses
Subject to the constitutional delaying procedure, after which the Assembly's will prevails
x: The Council cannot permanently veto an ordinary Bill passed by the Assembly. It may delay it for three months on the first occasion and one month on the second; thereafter the Assembly's will prevails.
tq: Track the delaying power rather than treating the Council's rejection as a veto.
sec: Assembly vs Council - money bills, ordinary bills, delaying power, no joint sitting

s: For how long can the Legislative Council delay an ordinary Bill passed by the Legislative Assembly on the first occasion and on the second occasion, respectively?
x: An ordinary Bill may be delayed by the Council for up to three months on the first occasion and one month on the second occasion.
tq: Keep the two successive delaying periods in their correct order.
sec: Assembly vs Council - money bills, ordinary bills, delaying power, no joint sitting

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Bill originating in the Legislative Council and rejected by the Legislative Assembly comes to an end.
2. The Legislative Council has no second chance to reconsider such a Bill.
3. A joint sitting can be summoned to resolve this disagreement in a State Legislature.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: a Bill originating in the Council ends when rejected by the Assembly, and there is no second chance for the Council. Statement 3 is false because State Legislatures have no provision for a joint sitting to resolve such a deadlock.
tq: Spot the Parliament–State Legislature confusion in the joint-sitting statement.
sec: Assembly vs Council - money bills, ordinary bills, delaying power, no joint sitting

s: Which one of the following statements regarding demands for grants in a State Legislature is correct?
o: Demands for grants are voted by the Governor after discussion in the Council.
The Legislative Council votes on demands for grants, while the Assembly only discusses them.
Demands for grants are voted only in the Legislative Assembly, while the Council may discuss them.
Both Houses vote jointly on demands for grants.
x: The Legislative Assembly alone votes on demands for grants. The Legislative Council may discuss them but cannot vote on them.
tq: Separate the power to discuss from the power to vote.
sec: Assembly vs Council - money bills, ordinary bills, delaying power, no joint sitting

s: Which one of the following correctly states the relative position of a State Legislative Council and the Rajya Sabha?
o: The State Council's power is essentially a delaying power and is weaker than that of the Rajya Sabha.
The State Council can dissolve the Legislative Assembly during a constitutional deadlock.
The State Council alone can ratify constitutional amendments.
The State Council has the same power as the Rajya Sabha to veto an ordinary Bill of the Assembly.
x: The State Legislative Council can delay legislation but cannot permanently veto an Assembly Bill. Its powers are considerably weaker than those of the Rajya Sabha in comparable matters.
tq: Avoid transferring the Rajya Sabha's powers to the State Council.
sec: Assembly vs Council - money bills, ordinary bills, delaying power, no joint sitting

s: Which statement concerning the representation of the Anglo-Indian community in State Legislative Assemblies is correct?
o: It was transferred to the Legislative Councils in 2020.
It was made compulsory in every State Assembly after 2020.
It continues without any constitutional change.
x: The constitutional provision for nomination of Anglo-Indian members to State Legislative Assemblies was discontinued in 2020.
tq: Test the time-bound constitutional change directly.
sec: Legislative Council composition - elected fractions, nominated, size, tenure

s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, the Legislative Council strength was prescribed as not more than 50 members for Andhra Pradesh and 40 members for Telangana. The permissible strength for Andhra Pradesh was subsequently raised to
x: Section 22(1) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act initially provided a ceiling of 50 members for Andhra Pradesh and 40 for Telangana. The 2015 Amendment Act raised Andhra Pradesh's permissible strength to 58.
tq: Distinguish the original ceiling from the figure introduced by the amendment.
sec: AP Legislature - 1956 strength, Assembly seats, Council strength, FIRST woman Speaker

s: Who is the present Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly?
x: Ch. Ayyanna Patrudu is the present Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly.
tq: Use the current office-holder carefully and distinguish it from the first woman Speaker.
sec: AP Legislature - 1956 strength, Assembly seats, Council strength, FIRST woman Speaker

s: The Governor notified the 2026 Monsoon Session of the Andhra Pradesh Legislature under Article 174(1), commencing on
x: The 2026 Monsoon Session of the Andhra Pradesh Legislature was notified to commence on 17 August 2026 under Article 174(1).
tq: Separate the date of notification from the date on which the session commenced.
sec: AP Legislature - 1956 strength, Assembly seats, Council strength, FIRST woman Speaker

s:
Consider the following statements regarding vacation of the office of the Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly:
1. The Speaker ceases to hold office if he or she ceases to be a member of the Assembly.
2. The Speaker may resign by addressing the resignation to the Deputy Speaker.
3. The Speaker can be removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the Assembly after fourteen days' notice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements correctly state the grounds and procedure for vacating the Speaker's office under Article 179.
tq: Check each procedural condition separately, especially the notice period and required majority.
sec: Speaker of the Legislative Assembly - powers, casting vote, Money Bill, resignation, vacating  [APPSC]

s: A resolution for the removal of the Speaker is under consideration in the Legislative Assembly. Which one of the following is correct?
o: The Speaker presides and has only a casting vote
The Speaker does not preside, but may speak and vote in the first instance
The Speaker must leave the House and cannot participate in the proceedings
The Speaker cannot speak but may vote in the second instance
x: Under Article 181, the Speaker does not preside while a resolution for removal is under consideration, but may speak and vote in the first instance.
tq: Apply the special procedural exception to the presiding officer's normal powers.
sec: Speaker of the Legislative Assembly - powers, casting vote, Money Bill, resignation, vacating  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following is NOT a power or function of the Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly?
o: Approving the creation of a Legislative Council in the State
Giving the final decision on whether a Bill is a Money Bill
Deciding disqualification under the Tenth Schedule, subject to judicial review
Adjourning or suspending the House in case of lack of quorum
x: The Speaker performs the first three functions. Creation or abolition of a Legislative Council involves an Assembly resolution followed by parliamentary law; it is not approved by the Speaker.
tq: Find the option assigning a constitutional function to the wrong authority.
sec: Speaker of the Legislative Assembly - powers, casting vote, Money Bill, resignation, vacating  [APPSC]

s: The Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly ordinarily exercises a casting vote when:
o: The House lacks the required quorum
A Bill is introduced for the first time
The Governor returns a Bill for reconsideration
There is equality of votes on a question before the House
x: Under Article 189, the Speaker does not vote in the first instance but exercises a casting vote in the event of an equality of votes.
tq: Distinguish the ordinary vote from the deciding or casting vote.
sec: Speaker of the Legislative Assembly - powers, casting vote, Money Bill, resignation, vacating  [APPSC]

s: After the dissolution of a State Legislative Assembly, the Speaker continues in office until:
o: The Council of Ministers recommends termination of the office
Just before the first meeting of the newly elected Assembly
The Governor appoints a new Speaker
The date on which the election results are declared
x: The Speaker continues after dissolution until immediately before the first meeting of the new Assembly.
tq: Watch the precise end-point in tenure questions rather than the general duration.
sec: Speaker of the Legislative Assembly - powers, casting vote, Money Bill, resignation, vacating  [APPSC]

s: When the office of the Speaker is vacant or the Speaker is absent, the Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly:
o: Acts with the full powers of the Speaker
Can only conduct voting on Money Bills
Requires prior permission of the Governor to preside
Is replaced by the Chairman of the Legislative Council
x: The Deputy Speaker acts with the full powers of the Speaker when the office is vacant or the Speaker is absent.
tq: Ask which officer legally substitutes for the principal presiding officer.
sec: Speaker of the Legislative Assembly - powers, casting vote, Money Bill, resignation, vacating  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 174 — Composition of the Legislative Council
Article 208 — Financial procedure and Annual Financial Statement
x: Article 168 deals with the constitution of State Legislatures. Article 172 concerns duration, Article 174 concerns sessions, and Article 208 concerns rules of procedure.
tq: Use article-number anchors and reject swapped constitutional subjects.
sec: Articles 168-212 - content  [APPSC]

s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below.

List-I (Article)
 a. 169
 b. 173
 c. 194
 d. 202

List-II (Subject)
 i. Qualifications for membership
 ii. Powers and privileges of State Legislatures
 iii. Creation or abolition of Legislative Councils
 iv. Annual Financial Statement
x: Article 169 concerns Legislative Councils, Article 173 qualifications, Article 194 privileges, and Article 202 the Annual Financial Statement.
tq: Start with the sure article-subject pair and eliminate codes containing a mismatch.
sec: Articles 168-212 - content  [APPSC]

s: Which Article provides for the duration of a State Legislative Assembly?
x: Article 172 deals with the duration of State Legislatures; the normal duration of the Legislative Assembly is five years unless sooner dissolved.
tq: Discriminate between adjacent constitutional provisions by their specific subject.
sec: Articles 168-212 - content  [APPSC]

s:
With reference to Articles 174 to 176, consider the following statements:
1. Article 174 deals with sessions, prorogation and dissolution of the State Legislature.
2. Article 175 deals with the Governor's right to address and send messages to the House or Houses.
3. Article 176 deals with the Governor's special address.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Articles 174, 175 and 176 respectively concern sessions and dissolution, the Governor's address and messages, and the special address.
tq: Read a sequence of neighbouring articles together instead of treating one article in isolation.
sec: Articles 168-212 - content  [APPSC]

s: The interval between the last sitting in one session of a State Legislature and the first sitting in the next session cannot exceed:
x: Article 174 requires that not more than six months intervene between the last sitting of one session and the first sitting of the next.
tq: Test the constitutional time limit directly and distinguish it from other legislative periods.
sec: Articles 168-212 - content  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 210 — Language to be used in the Legislature
Article 187 — Secretariat of the State Legislature
Article 194 — Powers and privileges of State Legislatures
x: Article 212 concerns the exclusion of judicial inquiry into legislative proceedings. The Annual Financial Statement is dealt with under Article 202.
tq: Locate the article-subject swap among otherwise familiar constitutional provisions.
sec: Articles 168-212 - content  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following statements regarding the State Legislature is correct?
1. Each House may make rules for regulating its procedure and conduct of business.
2. Courts cannot inquire into the proceedings of the Legislature merely on the ground of procedural irregularity.
3. Conduct of a High Court judge in the discharge of duties cannot be discussed in the State Legislature.
x: Articles 208, 212 and 211 respectively support the three statements.
tq: Combine related constitutional safeguards and identify the option containing all applicable provisions.
sec: Articles 168-212 - content  [APPSC]

s: The constitutional provision that no person can simultaneously be a member of both Houses of the Legislature of a State is contained in:
x: Article 190 provides, among other matters concerning vacation of seats, that a person cannot be a member of both Houses of a State Legislature at the same time.
tq: Match the specific membership restriction with its constitutional article.
sec: Articles 168-212 - content  [APPSC]

s: The normal order of proceedings at the beginning of a session of a State Legislative Assembly, as indicated for the State Legislature, is:
o: Voting on demands, Governor's address, general discussion
Governor's address, general discussion, voting on demands
General discussion, voting on demands, Governor's address
Governor's address, voting on demands, general discussion
x: The indicated order is the Governor's address, followed by general discussion and then voting on demands in the Assembly.
tq: Arrange the stages in the stated procedural sequence, not by constitutional article number.
sec: Articles 168-212 - content  [APPSC]

s: Under Article 169, the resolution of the Legislative Assembly seeking creation or abolition of a Legislative Council must be passed by:
o: A simple majority of members present and voting
A unanimous vote of all elected members
Two-thirds of the total membership of the Assembly
A majority of the total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting
x: The resolution requires a majority of the total membership of the Assembly and a majority of not less than two-thirds of members present and voting.
tq: Separate total-membership requirements from present-and-voting requirements.
sec: Article 169 - resolution majority, Parliament's role, Governor's role  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the law made by Parliament under Article 169:
1. Parliament passes the law by simple majority.
2. Such a law is deemed to be an amendment of the Constitution under Article 368.
3. Parliament determines the strength of the Legislative Council within the constitutional limits.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Parliament uses a simple majority and determines the Council's strength within the constitutional limits. The law is not deemed an amendment under Article 368, so statement 2 is false.
tq: Spot the constitutional-status trap in the statement that treats an ordinary law as an Article 368 amendment.
sec: Article 169 - resolution majority, Parliament's role, Governor's role  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the role of the Governor in the process under Article 169?
o: The Governor initiates the Assembly resolution for creation of the Council
The Governor alone can abolish the Legislative Council by notification
The Governor must approve the Assembly resolution before it is sent to Parliament
The Governor has no role in initiating or approving the resolution
x: The constitutional process is initiated by a special-majority resolution of the Legislative Assembly and completed through a law of Parliament; the Governor has no role in initiating or approving that resolution.
tq: Use the 'who would do this job?' test to reject powers wrongly assigned to the Governor.
sec: Article 169 - resolution majority, Parliament's role, Governor's role  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following correctly explains the relationship between the State Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council under Article 169?
o: The Council can abolish itself by a simple majority resolution
The Council can permanently prevent the Assembly from seeking its abolition
The Governor decides whether the Council should continue
The existence of the Council depends on the will of the Assembly, subject to parliamentary action
x: The Assembly may pass the required special-majority resolution, after which Parliament may enact the law. Thus, the Council's existence depends on the will of the Assembly expressed through this constitutional process.
tq: Trace the complete institutional chain instead of assigning the final power to the wrong body.
sec: Article 169 - resolution majority, Parliament's role, Governor's role  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 168 — Officers of the State Legislature
Articles 178 to 187 — Presiding officers and related offices of the State Legislature
Articles 202 to 207 — Judicial review of legislative proceedings
x: Articles 178 to 187 deal with the Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Chairman, Deputy Chairman and related legislative offices. The other pairs assign unrelated subjects to those provisions.
tq: Use the range of articles as a structural clue and reject broad subject swaps.
sec: Articles 168-212 - content  [APPSC]

s: The nominated representation in a State Legislative Council under Article 171 is:
x: The Governor nominates one-sixth of the members of the Legislative Council from specified fields under Article 171.
tq: Test a constitutional fraction directly and distinguish it from the elected categories.
sec: Articles 168-212 - content  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following statements about the Governor's addresses to the State Legislature is correct?
o: The Governor's address and special address are both optional
The Governor's special address is required at the first session after each general election and at the first session of each year
The Governor can address only the Legislative Council
The special address is required at the first session of every year
x: Article 176 provides for the Governor's special address at the first session after each general election and at the first session of each year.
tq: Distinguish the general power to address from the constitutionally required special occasions.
sec: Articles 168-212 - content  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following is the correct pairing of officers with the respective Houses of a bicameral State Legislature?
o: Speaker and Deputy Speaker — Legislative Assembly; Chairman and Deputy Chairman — Legislative Council
Chairman and Deputy Chairman — Legislative Assembly; Speaker and Deputy Speaker — Legislative Council
Speaker and Chairman — Legislative Assembly; Deputy Speaker and Deputy Chairman — Legislative Council
Governor and Speaker — Legislative Assembly; Chairman and Chief Minister — Legislative Council
x: The Assembly has a Speaker and Deputy Speaker, while the Council has a Chairman and Deputy Chairman.
tq: Discriminate between the similar titles used for the two Houses.
sec: Articles 168-212 - content  [APPSC]

s:
Assertion (A): The Speaker does not ordinarily vote in the first instance on a question before the Legislative Assembly.
Reason (R): The Speaker exercises a casting vote when there is an equality of votes.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Both statements are true. The casting vote on a tie is a separate rule and does not explain why the Speaker abstains from voting in the first instance.
tq: Separate two related rules from a genuine cause-and-effect relationship.
sec: Speaker of the Legislative Assembly - powers, casting vote, Money Bill, resignation, vacating  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with the subject covered by the indicated Articles?
o: Articles 190–193 — Vacation of seats and disqualification
Article 210 — Creation and abolition of Legislative Councils
x: Article 210 concerns the language to be used in the State Legislature. Creation and abolition of Legislative Councils is dealt with under Article 169.
tq: Find the one article-range pair that belongs to a different constitutional subject.
sec: Articles 168-212 - content  [APPSC]

s: Under Article 170 of the Constitution, the normal strength of a State Legislative Assembly shall be—
o: Not less than 60 and not more than 500 members
Not less than 50 and not more than 450 members
Not less than 70 and not more than 550 members
Not less than 40 and not more than 400 members
x: A State Legislative Assembly ordinarily consists of not less than 60 and not more than 500 directly elected members under Article 170.
tq: Use the constitutional minimum and maximum as the decisive numerical pair.
sec: Legislative Assembly - quorum, term, strength, non-Tenth Schedule disqualification, order of proceedings  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following States has a Legislative Assembly with 32 seats as a special constitutional exception?
x: Sikkim has 32 Assembly seats under the special provisions of Article 371F.
tq: Discriminate between the States having Assembly strength below the normal constitutional minimum.
sec: Legislative Assembly - quorum, term, strength, non-Tenth Schedule disqualification, order of proceedings  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the strength of State Legislative Assemblies:
1. Goa has 40 Assembly seats.
2. Mizoram has 40 Assembly seats.
3. Arunachal Pradesh has 60 Assembly seats despite its special constitutional minimum of 30.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Goa and Mizoram have 40 seats, while Arunachal Pradesh actually has 60 seats although Article 371H permits a minimum of 30.
tq: Separate the special minimum permitted by the Constitution from the actual present strength.
sec: Legislative Assembly - quorum, term, strength, non-Tenth Schedule disqualification, order of proceedings  [APPSC]

s: The normal term of a State Legislative Assembly is—
o: Five years from the date of notification of election results
Five years from the date appointed for its first meeting
Six years from the date of its constitution
Four years from the date of its first sitting
x: Under Article 172, the normal term of a State Legislative Assembly is five years from the date appointed for its first meeting, unless dissolved earlier.
tq: Distinguish the constitutional starting point of the term from election-related dates.
sec: Legislative Assembly - quorum, term, strength, non-Tenth Schedule disqualification, order of proceedings  [APPSC]

s: During a National Emergency, the term of a State Legislative Assembly may be extended by Parliament—
o: For six months at a time, but not beyond one year after the Emergency ends
For two years at a time, without any post-Emergency limit
For one year at a time, but not beyond six months after the Emergency ends
Indefinitely until Parliament revokes the Emergency
x: Parliament may extend the Assembly's term by one year at a time during a National Emergency, but the extension cannot continue beyond six months after the Emergency has ceased.
tq: Check both parts of the constitutional limitation: the interval and the post-Emergency ceiling.
sec: Legislative Assembly - quorum, term, strength, non-Tenth Schedule disqualification, order of proceedings  [APPSC]

s: In a Legislative Assembly consisting of 70 members, the quorum for a sitting would be—
x: Quorum is 10 members or one-tenth of the total membership, whichever is greater. For a 70-member House, 10 is greater than 7.
tq: Apply the ‘whichever is greater’ rule rather than simply calculating one-tenth.
sec: Legislative Assembly - quorum, term, strength, non-Tenth Schedule disqualification, order of proceedings  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the authority competent to decide a disqualification of a State legislator on grounds other than defection?
o: The High Court, on the recommendation of the Governor
The Governor, who is bound by the Election Commission's opinion
The Election Commission, whose decision is advisory to the Governor
x: Under Articles 191 and 192, the Governor decides such questions, but must act according to the opinion of the Election Commission. Defection matters are decided by the Speaker or Chairman.
tq: Ask who performs the formal decision and who supplies the binding constitutional opinion.
sec: Legislative Assembly - quorum, term, strength, non-Tenth Schedule disqualification, order of proceedings  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is NOT a ground of disqualification under Article 191 of the Constitution?
o: Being absent from the House for 60 days without permission
Being of unsound mind as declared by a competent court
x: Absence for 60 days without permission results in vacation of the seat under Article 190(4), not disqualification under Article 191.
tq: Distinguish disqualification under Article 191 from vacation of seat under Article 190.
sec: Disqualification of state legislators - Arts 191-192  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding disqualification under Article 191:
1. A person who is not a citizen of India may be disqualified.
2. Disqualification under a law made by Parliament may constitute a ground of disqualification.
3. Defection under the Tenth Schedule is included among the constitutional grounds.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three are grounds associated with Article 191. They include loss of citizenship, disqualification under parliamentary law such as the Representation of the People Act, and defection under the Tenth Schedule.
tq: Test the complete list of constitutional grounds instead of recalling only the common grounds.
sec: Disqualification of state legislators - Arts 191-192  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: A person elected to both Houses of a State Legislature is required to vacate one of the memberships because—
o: The Constitution prohibits simultaneous membership of both Houses of the same State Legislature
An MLA cannot become an MLC under any circumstances
The Council is a nominated body and cannot have elected members
The Governor alone may permit only one membership
x: Article 190 prevents a person from being a member of both Houses of the Legislature of a State at the same time. It also bars simultaneous membership of legislatures of two States.
tq: Use the constitutional incompatibility rule to eliminate explanations based on the composition of the Council.
sec: Disqualification of state legislators - Arts 191-192  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: Under Article 190(3)(b), the resignation of a member of a State Legislative Assembly takes effect only when—
o: It is accepted by the Speaker
It is accepted by the Governor
It is published in the official gazette
It is accepted by the Election Commission
x: The resignation of an MLA takes effect only upon acceptance by the Speaker. For a member of the Legislative Council, acceptance is by the Chairman.
tq: Match the resignation with the presiding officer of the concerned House.
sec: Disqualification of state legislators - Arts 191-192  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: If a member of a State Legislature remains absent without permission for 60 days, the consequence is—
o: Vacation of the seat under Article 190(4)
Suspension by the Governor under Article 192
Dissolution of the House under Article 172
x: Article 190(4) provides for vacation of the seat when a member remains absent without permission for 60 days, subject to the constitutional exclusions relating to periods when the House is prorogued or adjourned for more than four consecutive days.
tq: Identify the legal consequence instead of confusing absence with disqualification.
sec: Disqualification of state legislators - Arts 191-192  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: The rules governing the order of proceedings and conduct of business in a State Legislature are made under—
x: Article 208 deals with the rules of procedure of a State Legislature.
tq: Separate procedure-making provisions from provisions on term, quorum and disqualification.
sec: Legislative Assembly - quorum, term, strength, non-Tenth Schedule disqualification, order of proceedings  [APPSC]

s: With reference to the Governor's address to the State Legislature, which one of the following is correct?
o: It is delivered before every sitting of the Legislative Assembly.
It is delivered on the first day of the first session of each year and is followed by discussion.
It is delivered on the last day of every annual session.
It is delivered only when the Legislative Council demands it.
x: The Governor addresses the Legislature on the first day of the first session of each year, and the address is followed by discussion in the House.
tq: Use the time phrase ‘first day of the first session’ as the key discriminator.
sec: Legislative Assembly - quorum, term, strength, non-Tenth Schedule disqualification, order of proceedings  [APPSC]

s: In the budgetary proceedings of a State, demands for grants are voted only in the—
x: Demands for grants are voted exclusively by the Legislative Assembly. The Legislative Council has no power to vote on demands for grants.
tq: Identify the exclusive financial power of the directly elected House.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a valid statement regarding Article 191?
o: It empowers the Election Commission to directly remove a legislator from office.
It includes disqualification on the ground of being an undischarged insolvent.
It includes disqualification under a law made by Parliament.
It includes disqualification on the ground of holding an office of profit.
x: Article 191 lists grounds of disqualification, but the Election Commission does not directly remove the member. Under Article 192, the Governor decides the question on the Election Commission's opinion.
tq: Separate the grounds of disqualification from the authority that formally decides the question.

s:
With reference to the participation of MLAs in indirect elections, consider the following statements:
1. Elected MLAs are members of the electoral college for the election of the President.
2. MLAs elect members of the Rajya Sabha by proportional representation through the single transferable vote.
3. MLAs elect one-third of the members of the State Legislative Council.

x: All three statements are correct. Elected MLAs participate in the Presidential election, elect Rajya Sabha members by PR-STV, and elect one-third of the members of the State Legislative Council.

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the participation of State Legislative Assembly members in the elections of the President and Vice-President?

Elected MLAs vote in the Presidential election but not in the Vice-Presidential election.
Elected MLAs vote in both elections.
Neither elected nor nominated MLAs vote in either election.
x: Elected MLAs are part of the electoral college for the President under Article 54. The Vice-President is elected only by Members of Parliament, so MLAs do not participate.
tq: Discriminate between two similar indirect elections by identifying the composition of each electoral college.

Consider the following statements regarding the Telangana Legislative Council:

s: Which one of the following best describes the principal constitutional-democratic significance of a State Legislative Council?
o: It replaces the Legislative Assembly whenever the Council of Ministers resigns.
It exclusively controls the State’s financial legislation.
It directly appoints the Governor and the Chief Minister.
It checks hasty legislation and provides representation to experts who may not be able to face elections.
x: A Legislative Council acts as a revising chamber that can check hasty legislation and provide a place for experts who may not be able to secure election.
tq: Match the institutional function with the practical role of a revising chamber.

s: The criticism that a State Legislative Council is a costly ‘delaying chamber’ primarily relates to which of the following concerns?
o: It can permanently veto every Bill passed by the Legislative Assembly.
It alone possesses the power to introduce Money Bills in the State Legislature.
Its members are appointed entirely by the Union Government.
Its existence and effectiveness may depend heavily on the political strength of the ruling party in the Legislative Assembly.
x: Critics describe the Council as a costly delaying chamber because its political significance and continued existence may fluctuate with the ruling party’s position in the Assembly. It does not possess an absolute veto over Assembly legislation.
tq: Identify the institutional criticism without confusing delay with an absolute veto.
